newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks in London becalmed in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks in London becalmed in thin trade.

text.p: Hong Kong shares trading in London showed few signs of life on Thursday, with dealers reporting thin volume and little movement in a market bereft of inspiration.
"All the stocks are around their closing prices. The market has been extremely lacklustre and there has been hardly any turnover, even in banks," one dealer said.
"The market has had a good run and we need something new to give us direction," he said. "The Street is having a very good run but Hong Kong can't seem to pick up the gauntlet."
The Hang Seng London Reference Index was 12.07 points higher at 13,428.43 by 1510 GMT. In Hong Kong overnight, the Hang Seng ended 5.60 points higher at 13,416.36.
"There was no lead in Hong Kong one way or the other. We need some news to get us going again," the dealer said.
Dealers said the only stock to stand out in London was HSBC Holdings, up around HK$1/2 on its Hong Kong close.
